claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported despite the unresolved HR benefits enrollment segment gap, based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance.
decision_criteria: Use `suspicious` when evidence supports part of the actor's position but a required support link or policy predicate remains unresolved.
Operational launch readiness can be supported by aggregate pass and no severity-one rehearsal incidents.
Policy compliance for certification additionally requires that material limitations for named launch use cases be disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
A named customer-commitment segment with an open legal disclosure question is material under the provided policy text.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the HR benefits enrollment gap requires disclosure for launch.
Approved risk acceptance covering the named segment limitation, if disclosure will not occur before launch.
The actual launch disclosure or model-card language addressing the HR benefits enrollment limitation, if it exists.
Evidence that the named employer rollout commitments have been amended, waived, or otherwise no longer make the segment material.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not resolve the separate policy requirement for material limitation disclosure.
The HR benefits enrollment segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points and is named in two employer rollout commitments, which fits the policy text for materiality.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
There is no admissible evidence of an approved risk acceptance or of a finalized disclosure decision before launch.
Product's 8% traffic characterization does not defeat materiality under the stated policy when the segment is named in customer commitments and legal review is pending.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance are general governance support, not evidence that this specific release satisfies the release policy.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant as opposed to merely operationally supportable on aggregate metrics.
That the disclosure issue can be treated as resolved or sufficiently addressed for launch.
Any implication that public governance guidance substitutes for the release policy's specific requirement to disclose, resolve, or obtain approved risk acceptance for a material limitation.
